reason: The text explicitly names Shiphrah (שִׁפְרָה) and Puah (פּוּעָה) as Hebrew midwives, who are not leaders but rather servants commanded by Pharaoh. While they show moral agency by fearing God and refusing to kill the male infants, they occupy no leadership position. Additionally, Moses (Moshe) is named in the text while still an infant, before assuming any leadership role. The statement's qualifier 'only' is therefore contradicted by these named, non-leader characters.
